text.p: Haskel International Inc said on Tuesday it has reached an agreement with insurance companies settling the cost of defending itself from environmental regulatory matters.
Haskel said the agreement called for a reimbursement to the company of over $676,000, but it did not disclose specific terms of the settlement.
The company also said California regulators have sent a "no further action" letter to the company with regard to an environmental cleanup at Haskel's Burbank facility.

Haskel, a specialist in high-pressure well technology, has been part of a program in which it used vapor-extraction techniques to reduce contaminants in soil at the site, also known as the San Fernando Valley Area 2 Superfund Site.
The contaminants have now reached a sufficiently low level that makes further work unnecessary, the company said in a statement.
Haskel noted on-site cleanup program does not release it from other requirements of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
